operations.description:
Suspend a seller account, restricting their ability to create or edit products while maintaining access to process existing orders.

This operation is exclusively available to administrators and super administrators. When a seller account is suspended, all products from that seller are immediately hidden from search results and category listings. Customers cannot purchase products from suspended sellers. The suspended seller loses the ability to create new products or edit existing product listings.

However, suspended sellers retain the capability to process existing orders. This includes creating shipments with tracking information, shipping items to customers, and responding to cancellation and refund requests for their order items. This ensures customer orders are not disrupted by the suspension.

The suspension is tracked by setting the suspended boolean field to true on the seller account record. Administrators can later unsuspend the account using the corresponding unsuspend endpoint, which restores product visibility and full seller capabilities.

This operation is part of the seller management authority granted to administrators per the platform governance model. It provides a middle-ground enforcement mechanism between full account approval and permanent banning, allowing administrators to restrict seller activities while maintaining order fulfillment obligations.
operations.name: suspend
operations.specification:
Suspend a seller account by setting the suspended field to true on the shopping_mall_sellers table.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the requesting user has admin or superAdmin role
2. Query shopping_mall_sellers table by sellerId (UUID)
3. Validate seller exists and is not already suspended
4. Update the suspended field to true and updated_at timestamp
5. Create audit log entry for the suspension action
6. Return 204 No Content on success

Business rules enforced:
- While suspended, all products from this seller are hidden from search results and category listings (enforced at query level in product search endpoints)
- While suspended, products cannot be purchased (enforced at checkout validation)
- While suspended, seller cannot create new products (enforced at product creation endpoint)
- While suspended, seller cannot edit existing products (enforced at product update endpoint)
- While suspended, seller CAN still process existing orders including shipping items (shipment creation endpoint allows suspended sellers)
- While suspended, seller CAN still respond to cancellation and refund requests (cancellation/refund response endpoints allow suspended sellers)

Error scenarios:
- 404 Not Found: Seller ID does not exist
- 400 Bad Request: Seller is already suspended
- 403 Forbidden: Requesting user is not an administrator

parameters.description: Target seller account's ID (UUID format)
parameters.name: sellerId

Unsuspend a previously suspended seller account, restoring their full platform access and product visibility.

This operation is restricted to administrators and super administrators who have the authority to manage seller accounts. When a seller account is unsuspended, all products from that seller become visible again in search results and category listings. The seller regains the ability to create new products and edit existing products.

The seller account must currently be in suspended status for this operation to succeed. If the seller is already active (not suspended), the operation will return an error. This operation does not affect the seller's approval status - it only removes the suspension flag.

After unsuspension, the seller can immediately resume normal operations including product management, inventory updates, and order processing. Existing orders and order history remain unaffected by the suspension/unsuspension process.
operations.name: unsuspend

Query the shopping_mall_sellers table by the provided sellerId UUID parameter. Validate that the seller exists and is currently in suspended status (suspended = true). If the seller is not found or not suspended, return an appropriate error response.

Update the seller record by setting suspended = false and updated_at = current timestamp. This change immediately restores the seller's product visibility in search and category listings.

Return the complete updated seller profile including shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url, approval_status, and the updated suspended flag (now false). The response allows the administrator to confirm the unsuspension was successful.

Ensure this operation is protected by admin/superAdmin authorization middleware. Log the unsuspension action for audit purposes, including which administrator performed the action and when.

operations.description:
Ban a customer account, preventing the customer from logging in to the platform and accessing any authenticated features.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. When a customer account is banned, the system immediately terminates all active sessions for that customer and prevents any future login attempts using their credentials. The ban action is administrative and used for enforcing platform policies or responding to violations.

All existing orders placed by the banned customer are preserved in the system. The customer's order history remains accessible to administrators and sellers for fulfillment purposes. Past orders continue through their normal status workflow (PAID, SHIPPED, DELIVERED) even after the account is banned.

This operation is idempotent - banning an already-banned customer succeeds without error. To restore customer access, administrators must use the unban endpoint.

Related operations: POST /customers/{customerId}/unban to restore access, GET /admin/customers to view all customer accounts with their ban status.

Update the customer record to set the banned status flag. Terminate all active sessions for the customer by invalidating tokens in shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. Preserve all existing orders - do not modify shopping_mall_orders or shopping_mall_order_items. Return success response. Handle edge cases: customer not found (404), customer already banned (can proceed idempotently), requesting user not admin (403).

Restore a banned customer account's login access and platform privileges.

This administrator operation reverses a previous account ban, allowing the customer to log in with their existing credentials and access all platform features. When unbanned, the customer can immediately resume normal platform usage including browsing products, managing their cart, placing orders, and writing reviews.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. Regular customers and sellers cannot unban accounts. The customer's historical data including orders, reviews, wishlist, and addresses remain preserved throughout the ban period and are fully accessible after unbanning.

Existing orders placed before the ban remain in the system and continue through their normal status workflow. The customer's order history is preserved and accessible after account restoration.

Related operations:
- POST /admin/customers/{customerId}/ban - Ban a customer account
- PATCH /admin/customers - List all customer accounts with status filtering
- GET /admin/customers/{customerId} - View specific customer details
operations.name: unban

This operation unbans a previously banned customer account, restoring their ability to log in and access platform features.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the requesting user is an administrator (admin or superAdmin grade)
2. Query shopping_mall_customers table by customerId
3. Validate the customer exists and is currently banned
4. Update the customer's ban status to active (set banned flag to false or remove ban restriction)
5. Return the updated customer information

Business rules:
- Only administrators can execute this operation
- The customer account must exist and be in banned status
- Unbanning immediately restores login capability
- All existing orders and data remain preserved (they were never deleted)
- No notification is sent to the customer automatically

Edge cases:
- If customer is not banned: return error indicating account is already active
- If customer doesn't exist: return 404 not found
- If requester is not admin: return 403 forbidden

Database operations:
- SELECT from shopping_mall_customers WHERE id = {customerId}
- UPDATE shopping_mall_customers SET [ban_status_field] = false WHERE id = {customerId}

Note: The database schema shows deleted_at for soft deletion, but banning is a separate concern. The ban status field should be verified in the actual schema implementation.

operations.description:

When a seller account is banned, the seller cannot log in to the platform using their credentials. The authentication system will reject any login attempts from banned seller accounts.

Banning a seller account does not affect existing orders. All orders placed with the banned seller remain in the system and continue through their normal status workflow. The seller's shop name in past orders is preserved and remains visible to customers who purchased from them. Order items belonging to the banned seller continue through fulfillment, cancellation, and refund processes as normal.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. Regular customers and sellers cannot access this endpoint. Administrators can later unban the seller account using the corresponding unban endpoint, which restores the seller's login access and selling capabilities.

The ban action is immediate and takes effect upon successful completion. Any active sessions for the banned seller should be invalidated by the authentication system.

This DTO contains the credentials required for a seller to authenticate with the platform. The email and password are validated against the shopping_mall_sellers table, while the session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are captured from the HTTP request and recorded in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table for audit trail and security monitoring.

Upon successful authentication, the system generates JWT access and refresh tokens. Sellers with approval_status='PENDING' or 'REJECTED' can login to check their status but cannot perform seller operations requiring approval until approved by an administrator.
IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: Login request DTO for seller authentication. Maps email and password to shopping_mall_sellers table for credential validation. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are captured from HTTP request and stored in shopping_mall_seller_sessions table upon successful authentication. Backend validates: (1) Query by email, (2) Verify deleted_at is null, (3) Compare password using bcrypt against password_hash, (4) Check suspended is false, (5) Generate JWT tokens, (6) Create session record with connection metadata.

Contains an ordered array of image UUIDs where the first element becomes the main thumbnail displayed in product listings and search results. All active (non-deleted) images for the product must be included in the array - partial updates are not supported. The position of each image ID in the array determines its display order value.

Backend validates: (1) all IDs belong to the specified product from path parameter, (2) no duplicate IDs in array, (3) no missing active images (all images with deleted_at IS NULL must be included), (4) requesting user is seller who owns the product. Display order is computed from array position where index 0 maps to display_order 1, index 1 to display_order 2, etc. Before updating, create product snapshot to preserve previous image state for historical order references. Update shopping_mall_product_images.display_order for each image based on position. Return updated images array.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter DTO for session list filtering and pagination. Properties are not database columns but query filters: page/limit control pagination, status filters by expired_at comparison to NOW(), dateFrom/dateTo filter created_at range, sort controls ORDER BY clause. Backend applies these filters to the appropriate session table (shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_seller_sessions, etc.) based on authenticated actor type.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_images table for summary/list views. Maps id (UUID), image_url (imageUrl), display_order (displayOrder), and created_at (createdAt). Excludes updated_at (not needed for read-only summary), deleted_at (filtered by IS NULL in queries), shopping_mall_product_id (parent relation exposed through product context), and product relation (not needed in lightweight summary).
